# Plan a 3-day family weekend trip with ChatRTX in 15 minutes

> **In short:** ChatRTX is a free NVIDIA app running a private AI on your PC. Feed it your weekend details and it drafts a 3-day family itinerary, with restaurants and kid stops, in 15 minutes. It works offline, so it can't check live hours — verify those yourself.

Most AI travel planners live in the cloud, which means your family details travel with your question. ChatRTX is different: it's a chatbot that runs entirely on your own NVIDIA RTX graphics card, so nothing leaves your PC. You give it the basics — destination, who's coming, what you like — and it does the creative heavy lifting. This guide walks you through getting a working weekend plan out of it, even if you've never opened an AI tool before.

## Before you start
- **A Windows 11 PC with an NVIDIA RTX 30-series, 40-series, or newer GPU** with at least 8 GB of video memory. Older or non-RTX cards won't run it. Quick check: press **Win+R**, type `dxdiag`, and look under the "Display" tab.
- **About 50 GB of free disk space** for the app plus the AI model it downloads on first launch.
- **A free NVIDIA developer account** — you'll create one when you download the app.
- **Roughly 15 minutes** for the planning itself, plus longer the first time you install the app while it pulls the model down.

One honest note before you start: ChatRTX doesn't browse the web, so it can't tell you if a museum is open this Saturday. It drafts a plan from its training data; you confirm the time-sensitive bits yourself.

## Step 1 — Download and install ChatRTX
Open your browser and go to NVIDIA's official ChatRTX page. Look for a button labeled something like **"Download Now"** or **"Get ChatRTX"** and click it. NVIDIA asks you to sign in with a free account; create one in a couple of minutes if you don't have it yet. A file ending in `.exe` then downloads — open it and follow the installer, accepting the default folder. The installer is plain: keep clicking **Next** until it finishes. If your screen shows terms of service, tick the box and continue.
💬 Example: when the installer asks for the install location, leave the default `C:\Program Files\NVIDIA\ChatRTX` and click Next.
You'll know it worked when a new **ChatRTX** icon appears in your Start menu and the installer closes cleanly.

## Step 2 — Launch the app and pick a model
Click the **ChatRTX** icon to open the app. The very first launch takes a while because the app downloads an AI model — think of the model as the AI's "brain" that actually writes the answers. A small window shows the download progress as a percentage. When it's done, you'll see a chat screen with a model dropdown at the top. Pick any of the listed options (the names look like `Mistral` or `Llama 2`); all of them handle trip planning well. If your app jumps straight to an empty chat box, your model was already downloaded from a previous run — just start typing.
💬 Example: choose the first option in the list, which is usually labeled as the recommended default.
You'll know it worked when the chat box becomes active and you can click inside it to type.

## Step 3 — Tell ChatRTX the trip basics
Click into the chat box and write one short paragraph that covers where you're going, who's coming, and when. Don't overthink it — the more concrete you are, the better the plan. Mention ages if kids are coming, because "kid-friendly" means very different things for a 4-year-old and a 14-year-old. Press **Enter** to send. If the model dropdown reappears or shows a "loading" spinner, wait a few seconds before pressing Enter again.
💬 Example: "I'm planning a 3-day weekend trip to Asheville, North Carolina, leaving Friday afternoon. Our family is two adults, a 7-year-old, and a 10-year-old. We like short hikes, local food, and not too much driving each day."
You'll know it worked when ChatRTX replies with a short acknowledgment or a clarifying question within a few seconds.

## Step 4 — Ask for the day-by-day itinerary
Now ask for the actual schedule. Be specific about the format you want — a numbered list per day, with breakfast, lunch, dinner, and one or two activities. Keep the request to a single message so the answer stays focused. The AI may reply with a long block of text; that's normal and you can scroll. If the reply feels too short, send a follow-up that says "please expand Day 2 in more detail."
💬 Example: "Great. Please build a 3-day, day-by-day itinerary. For each day list morning, lunch, afternoon, dinner, and one kid-friendly stop. Keep driving under 30 minutes between activities."
You'll know it worked when the reply contains three labeled sections (Day 1, Day 2, Day 3) with food and activity suggestions in each.

## Step 5 — Add kid-friendly stops and refine
Read through what came back and pick one thing to improve. Send a follow-up that asks for more child-specific ideas, or swaps out something you don't like. A short, polite message works best — the AI takes you literally, so avoid sarcasm. If the answer feels too generic, give it a hint from your own life (a sport your kid plays, a treat they love) and ask it to weave that in. If the reply is cut off mid-sentence, just ask "please continue."
💬 Example: "On Day 2, my 7-year-old loves dinosaurs and my 10-year-old is into soccer. Can you suggest one stop for each that fits the same area?"
You'll know it worked when the new reply swaps in a specific kid-friendly stop — a science museum, a small zoo, a public field — without losing the rest of the day.

## Step 6 — Ask for restaurant ideas with a clear filter
Food is where ChatRTX's limits show. It can name places it was trained on, but it can't tell you if a restaurant is still open this weekend. Use it to brainstorm a short list of three to five options per meal, then check each one yourself on Google Maps or the restaurant's own site. Tell it your constraints — casual, kid-menu, walking distance — and ask for variety. If it suggests the same place twice, ask for "different options."
💬 Example: "Give me 4 casual dinner spots in downtown Asheville that are kid-friendly and don't require reservations. Mix of pizza, BBQ, and one healthier option."
You'll know it worked when you get a clean list of named restaurants, each with a one-line reason it fits your filter.

## Step 7 — Save your plan before you close the app
ChatRTX doesn't auto-save chats, so don't lose your work. The easiest method is to click anywhere inside the chat, press **Ctrl+A** to select everything, then **Ctrl+C** to copy. Open a new document in Word, Google Docs, or even Notepad, and paste the plan with **Ctrl+V**. Add your own notes on top — opening hours, reservations, the kid's nap time, an emergency pizza place. Give the file a name you'll remember later. If Ctrl+A doesn't select the chat text, click inside the chat area first and try again.
💬 Example: name the file `2026-Asheville-weekend-plan.docx` so it's easy to find next time you open your documents folder.
You'll know it worked when you can close ChatRTX, reopen the file, and read the full itinerary without needing the app.

## Common mistakes
- **Skipping the GPU check.** ChatRTX refuses to install on cards older than RTX 30-series. Always check `dxdiag` first so you don't sit through a failed download.
- **Expecting live data.** ChatRTX runs offline. It can't see today's weather, current opening hours, or live traffic. Use it to draft, then verify anything time-sensitive on Google Maps or the venue's site.
- **Asking for too much in one prompt.** A single massive request produces a vague answer. Splitting your planning into "day-by-day" and then "restaurants" (as in Steps 4 and 6) gives much sharper results.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** once you've used ChatRTX for one trip, the same workflow works for any plan that needs structure — birthday parties, weekly meals, study schedules. The skill is "ask in layers," not "ask the perfect question."
- **For your business or work:** because nothing leaves your PC, ChatRTX is a safe way to draft client-facing plans, internal agendas, or training outlines using your own notes without uploading anything to a cloud service.
- **If you're just getting started:** the very first run is the slowest because of the model download. After that, every chat starts fast. Don't judge the app by that first 30 minutes.

## Try it now
Open ChatRTX and type **"Plan a 3-day weekend trip for my family to [your nearest big city]. 2 adults, 1 kid age 6, we like parks and pancakes. Day-by-day please."** See what comes back in 30 seconds. Then follow Step 6 to add a restaurant shortlist and Step 7 to save it. Fifteen minutes, one solid plan.
